- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.40) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +3%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots next period — cap forecast at +2% above prior peak.
- If sentiment is consistently positive (e.g., > 0.30) and price is trending up, model underestimates continuation — add 2–5% to forecast mean.
- Model frequently overestimates short-term volatility — smooth 30d forecast by averaging last 7–10 days to reduce noise.
- When sentiment shifts from negative to positive, model lags in adjusting — delay forecast rise by 1–2 days relative to sentiment change.
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed, model tends to forecast mean-reversion — avoid sharp directional moves unless sentiment confirms trend.
- For 30d horizon, model often overpredicts near-term recovery — reduce forecast by 3–5% if sentiment is weak or mixed.
